title: Efficient Exploration Is Enough
abstract: arXiv:2609.07575v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: This work introduces an alternative view of efficient exploration and studies its theoretical and empirical implications in the absence of extrinsic rewards. Specifically, we define efficient explorers as agents that prioritize generating generalizable experience, i.e., data that supports learning models capable of predicting and adapting across the environment. This allows us to analyze efficient exploration through the lens of prediction and generalization. Theoretically, we demonstrate that optimally efficient explorers naturally schedule their trajectories to visit the most informative and learnable regions first. Empirically, we show that optimizing for these agents gives rise to an automatic curriculum of progressively more complex behaviors, even in relatively simple environments. translated_abstract: 这项工作提出了对高效探索的一种全新视角，并研究了其在缺乏外在奖励情况下的理论与实证意义。具体而言，我们将高效探索者定义为优先产生可泛化经验的智能体，即生成能够支持学习可跨环境进行预测和适应的模型的数据。这使我们能够通过预测和泛化的视角来分析高效探索。在理论上，我们证明了最优的高效探索者会自然地规划其轨迹，优先访问信息量最大且最可学习的区域。在实证上，我们表明对这些智能体进行优化会产生一个自动的课程，逐步生成更复杂的行为，即使在相对简单的环境中也是如此。这些结果表明，仅仅追求这种纯内在目标就足以驱动高度复杂行为的涌现。我们相信（摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 这篇论文证明了在无外在奖励的情况下，智能体若能高效地优先探索信息量最大、最可学习的区域以生成可泛化经验，仅凭这一纯内在目标就足以自动形成课程并涌现出高度复杂的行为。
en_tdlr: Pursuing purely intrinsic efficient exploration—prioritizing the generation of generalizable experience by visiting the most informative and learnable regions—is alone sufficient to yield automatic curricula and drive the emergence of highly sophisticated behaviors without extrinsic rewards.
